An image is provided at `/app/media/image.png`.

You may open, crop or zoom it as needed.

## Question

Look at the prominent red, white, and black striped flag hanging from the building on the left. Due to its position, can you tell what direction the wind is blowing?

## What to do

Write your answer to `/app/answer.md`.

**`/app/answer.md` is the only thing that is graded.** Nothing you print to the
terminal, and no other file, is read. If that file is missing or empty when you
stop, the task scores zero however good your analysis was.

You are working against a time limit and will be cut off without warning when it
is reached. So:

1. **Write a complete answer to `/app/answer.md` early** -- as soon as you have a
   defensible answer, before doing any deeper analysis.
2. Then investigate the media further and **overwrite the file** whenever your
   answer improves.

That way the file always holds your best answer so far, and being cut off costs
you refinement rather than the whole attempt. Answer in prose, and state each
point explicitly rather than implying it.

A flag works as a wind indicator only when the breeze is strong enough to lift
and extend the fabric: the flag then streams out *downwind*, so the fly end
points in the direction the wind is blowing toward, and the pole end shows where
it is coming from. That requires the flag to be held out away from its staff.

This flag is not extended at all, so there is no "pointing" direction to read.
A drooping flag is directionally ambiguous by definition — it would look exactly
the same whether the faint air movement was up the street, down the street, or
across it. Estimating a direction from it would be guesswork.

## What you *can* infer

You can infer the wind **strength**, even though you cannot infer its direction:
conditions were calm or nearly calm. On the Beaufort scale a completely limp,
vertically hanging flag corresponds to force 0 (calm) or at most force 1 (light

sunlight and sharp shadows, it reads as a still, warm, sunny day.

- Nothing on the pedestrian walking up the street — clothing, hair — is being
  pushed to one side.

## Bottom line

Because the striped flag is simply drooping down its pole under its own weight
rather than being blown out, the photograph gives no information about which way
the wind was blowing. It only shows that the wind was calm to negligible at that
moment.
